hypotheses.justification: The hypothesis `generated : IsWienerGenerated B` already implies it. `Malliavin.IsWienerGenerated.measurable` (IteratedIntegral.lean line 533) gives `Measurable (B t)` for every `t` from `generated`, with no other assumptions. Since `B t : W → ℝ` and ℝ is second countable, metrizable and has the Borel σ-algebra, `Measurable.stronglyMeasurable` turns this into `StronglyMeasurable (B t)`. So the proof can start with `have hsm : ∀ t, StronglyMeasurable (B t) := fun t => (generated.measurable t).stronglyMeasurable` and then proceed unchanged. The statement does not otherwise mention `hsm`, so deleting the binder leaves the statement as it was. It is true because `hsm` is derivable from `generated`.
